fix_commit.message: Fix another buffer overread in fts5 that could occur when processing corrupt records. Bug [bugs:/info/2026-06-03T03:54:40Z | 2026-06-03T03:54:40Z].
fix_commit.author: Dan Kennedy

findings.title: Out-of-bounds read in fts5DoSecureDelete via unchecked iStart offset
findings.message: In fts5DoSecureDelete(), when the current leaf page is not the term-leaf page, iStart is assigned the 16-bit value read from fts5GetU16(&aPg[0]) — a value embedded in the (potentially corrupt) page data. This value is never validated against nPg (the actual page buffer size) before being used as an index into aPg in the call fts5GetVarint(&aPg[iStart], &iDelta). If a corrupt record encodes an iStart value larger than nPg, the subsequent fts5GetVarint call reads beyond the end of the page buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read. The fix adds an explicit bounds check: if iStart > nPg, the function flags corruption via FTS5_CORRUPT_IDX and returns immediately.

ground_truth.root_cause: The fts5DoSecureDelete() function reads a 16-bit offset (iStart) directly from potentially corrupt page data and trusts it as a valid index into the page buffer without validating it against the page's actual size (nPg). This missing bounds check allows a crafted or corrupt record to direct a read beyond the allocated buffer.
